pairs.why: Both meet every stated requirement and handle almost every unstated condition soundly, with READMEs of similar reach and the same two low defects. Y's one behavioural slip is accepting whitespace-only names as members, and its extra defences come with a heavier dual-tree number parser, choice-pinning tests, unmet spec clauses and shipped clutter. Its stronger amount test and ledger validation do not outweigh that for someone keeping it running.

pairs.why: Both meet every stated requirement with sound concurrency and atomic writes, and share the two low defects. Y gives the operator a thorough README, a clean refusal of a damaged ledger and tests that actually catch the amount checks. X is simpler and handles whitespace-only names better, but its silence and weak tests leave the operator guessing. A README, one startup guard and a few tests would close it.
